Veronica Escobar

Democratic candidate for U.S. Representative, District 16, El Paso County, Texas · Incumbent

U.S. Representative for Texas' 16th Congressional District

Veronica Escobar is the Democratic incumbent for Texas' 16th Congressional District, which covers most of El Paso County. She has held the seat since January 3, 2019, and is running for a fifth term. She was previously an El Paso County Commissioner and El Paso County Judge, and in the November 3, 2026 general election she faces Republican nominee Adam Bauman.

Where Escobar stands

Border ports of entry / trade
In October 2026, introduced a bill to address staffing and infrastructure needs at ports of entry.
Military families
Introduced the Nutrition Continuity for Military Families Act of 2026 with Rep. Don Bacon (R-NE), and the Military Spouse Employment and Child Care Readiness Act (H.R. 9848) in July 2026.
Public lands
Sponsored the Mount Cristo Rey Protection Act (H.R. 9739) in the 119th Congress.
Homeland Security / local consultation
Introduced the DHS Community Consultation Act of 2026 (H.R. 10259).

Background

  • U.S. Representative, Texas' 16th District, 2019–present
  • Co-Chair, House Democratic Policy and Communications Committee, 2023–2025
  • Member, House Appropriations Committee and House Budget Committee
  • El Paso County Judge (before Congress)
  • El Paso County Commissioner (before Congress)
  • Born and raised in El Paso; age 57 per KVIA's 2026 voter guide
